Yes — to me that's plainly the same article, and I'd want the app to recognize it as the one I already saved rather than making a second copy.

The way I think about it: that "?utm_source=newsletter" bit is just tracking gunk that got tacked on because I clicked through from an email, and the "#comments" is only telling the page to scroll down to the comments — neither one changes *what* the page is. It's the same story either way. If I've already saved it, pasting the dressed-up version should just walk me back to my existing card, the same friendly way it did when I re-pasted an identical link earlier — ideally dropping me into editing it, so if I meant to update something I'm right there.

The one thing I'd gently ask: be careful only to ignore the stuff that's genuinely just noise like that. If a web address uses something after the "?" to point at a genuinely different page, that's a real difference and shouldn't be collapsed into another bookmark. But for tracking tags and a jump-to-section like these, yes — treat it as the same one and take me back to it.
